blocks.content:
• SEBI is NOT constitutional.
• Became statutory in 1992.
• RBI has one member on SEBI board.
• Prevents insider trading.
• Regulates mutual funds and intermediaries.

items: Exam Trap: Questions frequently test whether SEBI is constitutional. Remember it is STATUTORY (1992), NOT constitutional.
Board Composition Trap: Remember that RBI has exactly ONE member on the SEBI board.
Regulatory Scope: SEBI regulates both mutual funds and intermediaries while working to prevent insider trading.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI is a non-constitutional body that became statutory in 1992.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has one representative member on the SEBI board.
SEBI actively prevents insider trading in capital markets.
SEBI regulates financial market intermediaries and mutual funds.
